source_text: μαρτύρια, καὶ τίς ἡ ξύλων ἀσήπτων γέγονε χρεία. Τί δ' ἂν βούλοιτο δηλοῦν, καὶ τῇ κιβωτῷ τὸ χρυσίον, τὰ τέως ἐν τάξει χρείας τε καὶ κόσμου συντεθειμένα, κυμάτια δὴ λέγω, στρεπτὰ, κρίκους τε καὶ ἀναφορέας, εἰ περιεργάζοιτο τυχὸν, σκληρὸν εὑρήσει τὸ χρῆμα. Καὶ λόγον αὐτοῖς ἐφαρμόσαι τὸν μυστικὸν οὐκ ἔχων, περιττοεπήσει τάχα που, καὶ ὄχλον εἰκαίων ἐπισωρεύσει ῥημάτων, ταῖς τῶν φιλομαθεστέρων ἀκοαῖς. Ἀληθὴς δὲ ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος οὐκ ἐπί τοι μόνης τῆς κιβωτοῦ τυχὸν, προσθείην δ' ἂν ὅτι καὶ ἐπί γε τῶν ἄλλων, ἃ δὴ γενέσθαι προστέταχεν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὐκ ἀπίθανά μοι δοκεῖς διανοεῖσθαί τε καὶ λέγειν. Τοιγάρτοι μεθεὶς τό γε ἧκον, ὡς φὴς, εἰς συμμετρίαν. τε καὶ χρείαν, ἤγουν εἰς κόσμον τῶν ἀποτελεσμάτων, ἐπ' αὐτὸ διᾴττειν ἐπείγου τὸ τοῖς θεωρήμασιν, ἀναγκαῖον, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τίνα τρόπον αὐτὸς ἡμῖν ὁ Χριστὸς σημαίνεται διὰ τῶν παραδεδειγμένων, ἤτοι κατεσκευασμένων, ἀμελητὶ διασάφει. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν, ἐγὼ μὲν, ὡς ἔνι φράσαι τε καὶ νοεῖν, πειράσομαι. Διαμαρτάνοντι δέ τ' ἀληθοῦς, καὶ μεῖον ἢ χρὴ τῇ τῶν νοημάτων ὑπεροχῇ προσβάλλοντι, συγγνώμων ἔσο. Τὸ γὰρ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ τε καὶ αἰνίγματι βλέπειν, ἀποσφήλειεν ἂν ἔσθ' ὅτε καὶ τὸν ἀκριβῆ τε καὶ ἔμφρονα νοῦν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ λέγεις. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἡ κιβωτὸς ἡμῖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τύπος ἂν εἴη καὶ εἰκὼν τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Τὸν γὰρ τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως τοῦ Μονογενοῦς ἀνασκοπούμενοι τρόπον, καθάπερ ἐν κιβωτῷ τῷ ἐκ Παρθένου ναῷ τὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς Λόγον ἐνηυλισμένον ὀψόμεθα. «Κατῴκησε γὰρ ἐν αὐτῷ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος σωματικῶς,» κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Λόγος δὲ ἦν Θεοῦ, τὰ ἐν τῇ κιβωτῷ μαρτύρια. Καὶ ἄσηπτα μὲν ἦν αὐτῆς τὰ ξύλα, χρυσῷ δὲ τῷ καθαρῷ καὶ δοκιμωτάτῳ κατεκαλλύνετο, ἔσωθέν τε καὶ ἔξωθεν. Ἄφθαρτον γὰρ τὸ σῶμα Χριστοῦ, καθάπερ τινὶ χρυσῷ, τῇ τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος Λόγου δυνάμει καὶ λαμπρότητι, καὶ τῇ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος φύσει καὶ ἐνεργείᾳ ζωοποιῷ, πρὸς ἀφθαρσίαν διακρατούμενον. Διὰ γάρ τοι τοῦτο καὶ ζωοποιεῖν λέγεται Χριστός. Ζωὴ γὰρ ὢν κατὰ φύσιν ὁ ἐκ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς Λόγος, τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ ἰδίου πνεύματος τὸν ἴδιον αὐτὸς ἀνεζωοποίει ναὸν, φθορᾶς ἀνωτέρω τιθείς. «Ἡ γὰρ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ οὐκ οἶδε διαφθορὰν,» κατὰ τὴν τοῦ ἁγίου Παύλου φωνήν. Προσεφώνει δέ που καὶ Ἰουδαίοις, περὶ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος· «Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν·» καὶ μὴν καὶ ὁ Πέτρος τεθανατῶσθαι μὲν σαρκὶ, φησὶν, αὐτὸν, ἐζωοποιῆσθαι δὲ πνεύματι. Σύμβολον οὖν ἄρα τῆς ὑπερλάμπρου θεότητος, ὁ χρυσὸς, ἐπαληλειμμένης ὥσπερ τῷ ἁγίῳ σώματι, καὶ τὴν ἰδίαν αὐτοῦ λαμπρότητά τε καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν ἐνιείσης ἀποῤῥήτως, καὶ ὡς αὐτή που μόνη καὶ καθ' ἑαυτὴν ἡ θεία τε καὶ ὑπὲρ νοῦν ἐπίσταται φύσις. Εἰ γὰρ «Οἱ δίκαιοι κατὰ
pass_a_gloss: [cont. from s5: he will find what the ark (κιβωτός) is and the things in it,] the testimonies (μαρτύρια), and what need (χρεία) there was of unrotting woods (ξύλα ἄσηπτα). But what the gold (χρυσίον) on the ark would wish to show (δηλοῦν), and the things put together for the time being (τέως) in the order of use and ornament (χρεία, κόσμος) — I mean mouldings (κυμάτια), twisted work (στρεπτά), rings (κρίκοι), carrying poles (ἀναφορεῖς) — if he should busy himself (περιεργάζομαι) with them, he will find the thing hard (σκληρός). Not having a mystical account (λόγος μυστικός) to fit (ἐφαρμόζω) to them, he will over-talk (περιττοεπέω) and heap up a crowd of random words (ὄχλος εἰκαίων ῥημάτων) on the ears of the more studious (φιλομαθέστεροι). Our word is true not only of the ark; I would add, also of the other things he commanded (προστάσσω) to be made. PALL: You seem to think and say not unpersuasive things (οὐκ ἀπίθανα). So letting go what reaches, as you say, to proportion (συμμετρία) and use, or to ornament of the finished works (ἀποτελέσματα), hasten to dart (διᾴττω) to what is necessary for the contemplations (θεωρήματα): in what manner Christ himself is signified (σημαίνεται) to us through the things shown in pattern (παραδεδειγμένα), or constructed (κατεσκευασμένα); explain without hesitation (ἀμελητί). CYR: I will try, as it is possible to say and conceive. To one who misses the truth and attacks (προσβάλλω) less than needed the loftiness (ὑπεροχή) of the meanings, be forgiving (συγγνώμων). For seeing in a mirror and riddle (ἔσοπτρον, αἴνιγμα) can trip up (ἀποσφάλλω) sometimes even the exact and sensible mind (νοῦς). PALL: Well said. CYR: The ark would be for us a type and image (τύπος, εἰκών) of Christ. Considering the manner of the Only-begotten's becoming man (ἐνανθρώπησις τοῦ Μονογενοῦς), we shall see the Word from God the Father lodged (ἐναυλίζομαι), as in an ark, in the temple from the Virgin (ναὸς ἐκ Παρθένου). 'For all the fullness of the Godhead (πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος) dwelt in him bodily (σωματικῶς).' The testimonies in the ark were Word/word of God (Λόγος). Its woods were unrotting, adorned (κατακαλλύνω) with pure and most tested (δοκιμώτατος) gold inside and out. For Christ's body is incorruptible (ἄφθαρτον), held fast (διακρατέω) toward incorruption (ἀφθαρσία), as by gold, by the power and brightness (δύναμις, λαμπρότης) of the indwelling Word, and by the nature and life-giving working (φύσις, ἐνέργεια ζωοποιός) of the Holy Spirit. Therefore Christ is said to give life (ζωοποιεῖν). For the Word from God the Father, being Life by nature (ζωὴ κατὰ φύσιν), by the power of his own spirit (ἴδιον πνεῦμα) himself re-vivified (ἀναζωοποιέω, impf.) his own temple, placing it above corruption (φθορά). 'For his flesh knows (οἶδε) not corruption (διαφθορά),' per holy Paul. He addressed the Jews about his own body: 'Destroy (λύσατε) this temple, and in three days I will raise (ἐγερῶ) it.' And Peter says he was put to death in flesh, made alive in/by spirit (πνεύματι). So the gold is a symbol (σύμβολον) of the over-bright Godhead (ὑπέρλαμπρος θεότης), smeared over (ἐπαλείφω) as it were the holy body, and sending into it ineffably (ἀποῤῥήτως) his own brightness and incorruption, as only the divine nature beyond mind (ὑπὲρ νοῦν φύσις) itself by itself knows (ἐπίσταμαι). For if 'the righteous in due [times]' [cont. in s7].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the testimonies, and what need there was for wood that does not rot. But if he should perhaps pry closely into what the gold on the ark is meant to show, and into the things put together for the time being for use and ornament, I mean the mouldings, the twisted work, the rings and the carrying poles (Exodus 25:11–14), he will find the matter hard. Unable to fit a mystical sense to them, he will probably say more than is needed and pile a mass of idle words on the ears of those keener to learn. And what I say holds true, perhaps, not of the ark alone; I would add that it holds also of the other things he commanded to be made.

Palladius: Your thinking and your words seem to me not unconvincing. So set aside what concerns, as you say, proportion and use, that is, the ornament of the finished works, and hurry straight to what our contemplation needs: explain without hesitation in what way Christ himself is signified to us by the things shown as a pattern, that is, the things that were built.

Cyril: Well then, I will try, as far as one can speak and understand. But if I miss the truth, and reach less than I ought toward the height of these thoughts, be forgiving. For seeing in a mirror and in a riddle (1 Corinthians 13:12) can at times trip up even a precise and sensible mind.

Cyril: The ark, Palladius, would be for us a type and image of Christ. For when we look closely at the manner in which the Only-begotten became man, we shall see the Word who is from God the Father dwelling, as in an ark, in the temple that is from the Virgin. For ‘all the fullness of the Godhead dwelt in him bodily’ (Colossians 2:9), as the Scriptures say. And the testimonies in the ark were the Word of God. Its wood did not rot, and it was adorned inside and out with pure and thoroughly tested gold (Exodus 25:10–11). For the body of Christ is incorruptible: it is held fast in incorruption, as by a kind of gold, by the power and radiance of the Word who dwells in it, and by the nature and life-giving working of the Holy Spirit. That is why Christ is also said to give life. For the Word who is from God the Father, being Life by nature, himself brought his own temple back to life by the power of his own Spirit, setting it above corruption. For ‘his flesh knows no corruption,’ in the words of holy Paul (Acts 13:37; Acts 2:31). And he also told the Jews somewhere, speaking of his own body, ‘Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up’ (John 2:19); and Peter, too, says that he was put to death in the flesh but made alive in the Spirit (1 Peter 3:18). So the gold is a symbol of the surpassingly bright Godhead, laid over the holy body, as it were, and instilling in it, beyond telling, his own brightness and incorruption, in a way known only to the divine nature itself, which is beyond understanding. anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-sentence (continues s5 'he will perhaps find what the ark is, and the things in it'); label 'Cyril: …' kept as in the rest of Book 9. Ends mid-quotation of Matthew 13:43 ('Οἱ δίκαιοι κατὰ | καιροὺς'); the citation stands in s7 where the quotation closes. τέως ('for the time being') rendered as such: the fittings served the tabernacle's use and ornament, not a mystical sense. Source has a stray period in 'συμμετρίαν. τε' (OCR); read as συμμετρίαν τε. παραδεδειγμένα echoes the 'pattern shown' of Exodus 25:9, 40 but is vocabulary, not a quotation: uncited. Λόγος δὲ ἦν Θεοῦ: Migne capitalises; the double sense (the tablets as God's word, and the Word within the temple of the body) is intended, so 'the Word of God' is kept with capital W. 'his own Spirit' (τοῦ ἰδίου πνεύματος, lower case in Migne): capitalised because Cyril has just named the Holy Spirit and regularly calls the Spirit the Son's own. Colossians 2:9: Cyril has aorist κατῴκησε ('dwelt') for NT present κατοικεῖ. 'His flesh knows no corruption': Cyril credits Paul, so Acts 13:37 (Paul at Pisidian Antioch, 'did not see corruption') is cited first; the wording ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ matches Peter at Acts 2:31, so both are cited inline (both quote Psalm 16:10, LXX 15:10); οἶδε may be itacism for εἶδε ('saw'). 'περὶ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος' echoes John 2:21 (part of the John 2:19 context, not separately cited). 1 Peter 3:18 πνεύματι rendered 'in the Spirit', which keeps Cyril's instrumental reading open without forcing it. 'τὴν ἰδίαν αὐτοῦ λαμπρότητα': αὐτοῦ (masc./neut.) cannot refer to θεότης (fem.); taken as the Word's own brightness, hence 'his own'. 'Life by nature' may echo John 11:25 / 14:6 but no clear quotation: uncited. 'Christ is said to give life' may recall John 5:21; doubtful, uncited.

changes: Removed doubled parentheses around the list of fittings; συντεθειμένα now 'put together'
'heap a crowd of idle words' (calque of ὄχλον) -> 'pile a mass of idle words'; τάχα που 'probably'
ἤτοι rendered 'that is', not 'or rather' (no correction implied); ἀμελητί 'without hesitation'
'temple taken from the Virgin' -> 'temple that is from the Virgin' (no 'taken' in Greek)
Citation 'his flesh knows no corruption' now (Acts 13:37; Acts 2:31): Cyril names Paul, wording is Acts 2:31
Last clause smoothed: 'known only to the divine nature itself' (μόνη καὶ καθ' ἑαυτήν) without the doubled 'only... alone'
